subject: Intermittent token emission slowdown affecting live chat — customer steps & next actions
messages:
From: Rachel Kim <rachel@stratonics.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 10 Jun 2029 09:12:42 -0700
Subject: Live chat slowdowns today — tokens emitting in long pauses

Hi Lauren,

We're seeing an intermittent problem this morning where our user-facing live chat sessions built on your streaming API are returning long pauses during generation (sometimes 6-12s gaps between chunks). This started around 08:30 PDT and has affected about 8% of our sessions — primarily in US-West. Our telemetry shows the client socket remains open, but token chunks are delayed; there are no obvious client-side errors.

I've attached a small sample of request IDs and timestamps. Can your team confirm whether there are known issues on your side and any short-term mitigations we can apply? This is impacting our checkout-assist flow so we need a workaround ASAP.

Thanks,
Rachel
Rachel Kim
Head of Integrations, Stratonics
ops@stratonics.com

Attachment: stratonics_sample_request_ids.txt (text, 2 KB)

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel@stratonics.com>
Cc: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 10 Jun 2029 09:38:10 -07:00
Subject: Re: Live chat slowdowns today — tokens emitting in long pauses

Hi Rachel — thanks for the report and the sample IDs. We're actively triaging. Initial notes & immediate steps you can try now to reduce user impact: 

1) Temporarily switch to the non-streaming (complete) endpoint for the checkout-assist route for sessions with <= 512 tokens expected — this avoids chunking latency and is usually faster when token emission stalls.
2) If you need to continue streaming, lower the chunk size (max_tokens per chunk) to 32 and add a client-side 250ms jittered retry on missing chunk after 1.5s.
3) Reduce response window (max_new_tokens) from 1024 to 512 for peak periods to reduce KV cache pressure on the edge.
4) As a short-term routing change, set region=us-east if your clients are distributed; we have more headroom there while we investigate us-west hotspots.

We've opened SR-1789 internally and attached a mitigation checklist and log-extract request so we can correlate. Jonas/Logan: tagging you for SRE attention to check in-flight queue depth and edge proxy backpressure in us-west-2.

I'll follow up with a timeline for the root cause once SRE has initial findings. For immediate credit/compensation requests please indicate impacted time window and if you'd like priority remediation.

Best,
Lauren Bishop
Director, Customer Success
Redwood Inference
lauren.bishop@redwood.com

Attachments: mitigation-checklist.pdf (PDF, 48 KB)

From: Site Reliability <sre@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 10 Jun 2029 09:56:03 -07:00
Subject: [SRE] Preliminary: token emit backlog on edge shards us-west-2

Team,
We've identified transient backlog growth in the token emission queues on a subset of edge shards serving us-west-2 between 08:20-09:00 PDT. Root cause candidate: a mis-optimized kernel selection combined with a spike in long-sequence requests that pushed the per-instance batching window above target. This produced delayed flushes and increased tail latency for streaming.

Immediate actions taken:
- Scaled additional edge shard capacity in us-west-2 and triggered a rolling restart of affected hosts.
- Decreased the batching window for long-sequence models to 30ms from 100ms for the hot shard pool.
- Enabled a temporary fallback route to compatible quantized variants for susceptible requests.

Requesting sample request IDs from Rachel (attached) to correlate traces and token-level timing. We will keep the customer updated and prepare a post-incident summary.

-JS (on-call SRE)

Jonas
We'll continue monitoring; tagging this to the SR-1789 ticket. I attached the extracted logs for Rachel's sample IDs in case she wants raw timing data.

Attachment: sr-1789-log-extracts.zip (zip, 3.2 MB)

We saw the affected sessions drop from ~8% to ~0.7% and response fidelity remained acceptable.

Can you share the post-incident write-up and proposed credit for the 90-minute window where our checkout flow was degraded? We'd also like any recommended long-term config changes for our workload profile (50% of sessions long-form, 50% short) so we can optimize going forward.
